_comment: Franchises TMDB groups badly, curated by hand. Only exceptions belong here:
anything TMDB's own collection gets right is offered automatically from that
collection, so John Wick, Pirates of the Caribbean and Jurassic Park need no
entry and stay correct on their own as films are added.
no entry. Every id below was resolved from TMDB rather than typed, and the
candidates came from tools/detect_franchises.py, which flags franchises whose
films land in more than one collection or sit outside the one they belong to.
Entries are matched by tmdb_id, so a search for any member offers the whole
franchise. title and date are for reading this file; the app takes both from
TMDB at render time, so they can drift without breaking anything.
Why each of these is here, and where a judgement call was made:
Marvel           the whole Marvel catalogue, matching the scope the watchlist
sites cover: the MCU, the Fox and Sony films, the Netflix and
ABC shows, the animated series and the One-Shots. Built from
TMDB's Marvel companies plus the MCU list, because no single
query returns it — the MCU keyword gives 80 films and Marvel
Studios as a company gives 103, Raimi's Spider-Man and a
comics documentary included.
The only franchise with tiers: 169 titles is too many to open
flat. The tier picks are ours, not taken from anyone's site —
they are judgements, and live here so they can be edited.
A title in two lists resolves to the smaller one, so Logan
opens the fourteen X-Men films rather than all of Marvel.
Alien            four TMDB collections (Alien, Prometheus, Romulus, AVP), plus
a TV series TMDB files under no franchise at all
Middle-earth     The Hobbit is a separate collection from The Lord of the Rings,
and War of the Rohirrim sits outside both
Spider-Man       four collections (Raimi, Amazing, MCU, Spider-Verse). Sony's
Venom/Morbius films are left out: no Spider-Man in them
Batman           five collections. Live-action, Batman-led films only — the
DCEU ensembles are not Batman films, and the animated canon
is a different and much larger thing
X-Men            X-Men and Wolverine are separate collections; Deadpool sits
outside both. The whole Fox run, ending with the MCU crossover
The Hunger Games split into the original collection and a 'New Trilogy' one
Star Wars        The Clone Wars, Rogue One and Solo sit outside the collection,
and the series are in no collection at all. This one is the
whole canon rather than a shortlist — films and every series,
animated included, down to the 1978 Holiday Special and the
Ewok films — so someone new to it has one list in release order
Harry Potter     TMDB gets this one right; kept as the worked example from the
spec, and harmless because curated entries merge with TMDB
Animation is the one list here that is not a franchise: it is every animated
feature the big studios have released, for "have I seen all of these". It is
generated by tools/build_animated.py (re-run it when a film comes out) and
kept to released theatrical features — the runtime comes from TMDB's details
endpoint, because discover's own runtime filter waves 21-minute TV specials
through. Being broad, it sorts behind every specific list a title also sits
in, so searching Shrek still offers the four Shrek films first.
The anime franchises below are generated by tools/build_anime_franchises.py
(re-run it when a season or a film lands). They exist because TMDB files a
franchise's parts as unrelated shows and collections: Naruto, Shippuden and
Boruto are three shows, Fate is nine, and the films sit in collections of
their own or in none. Ranked by MyAnimeList membership with a franchise's
entries summed, which is the only honest reading of "most popular franchise";
the long-runners are kept by name because that sum under-counts them, their
popularity being spread over dozens of entries.
A franchise needs two parts to be worth a list. Frieren and Dandadan have one
season each on TMDB and no films, so they are left out until they do not.
Series are one entry per aired season, dated by that season. TMDB's own
seasons are kept as TMDB has them — where it has merged two cours the app
sorts it out, and splitting them here would fight that. Bleach is the worked
example: TMDB keeps Thousand-Year Blood War as season 2 of Bleach (30984),
not as a show of its own.
